title: Sections of split-torus extensions over local rings
statement: Let $C$ be a nonzero commutative local ring, meaning a ring with a unique maximal ideal, and put $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $E$ and $J$ be commutative group schemes over $U$ [def-pc-scheme]: their multiplication, identity and inverse morphisms satisfy the commutative group diagrams. Let $r\geq0$ and put $T=\mathbf G_{m,U}^{r}$, where $\mathbf G_{m,U}=\operatorname{Spec}C[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. Suppose $1\to T\xrightarrow{i}E\xrightarrow{q}J\to1$ is exact as a sequence of fppf sheaves [def-pc-fppf-site]: $i$ identifies $T$ with the scheme-theoretic kernel and sections of $J$ lift fppf locally to $E$. For a $U$-scheme $Y$, write $Y(C)=\operatorname{Hom}_U(U,Y)$. Then $q:E(C)\to J(C)$ is surjective. This includes the case where $C$ is a field.

source.place: Tag 03P8 (theorem-picard-group), including fppf cohomology; groupoids.tex Tags 0499 (lemma-characterize-trivial-pseudo-torsors) and 049A (definition-principal-homogeneous-space). Agent-extracted local-ring, finite-product consequence; each line module on the spectrum of a local ring is trivial.

proof.text: Fix $j\in J(C)$ and form $P=E\times_{J,j}U$. By the fibre-product universal property, its sections over $V\to U$ are precisely $e\in E(V)$ with $q(e)=j|_V$. Translation by $i(t)$ defines a $T$-action on $P$. If $p,p'\in P(V)$, then $q(p'p^{-1})=1$, so the given identification $T=\ker q$ gives a unique $t\in T(V)$ with $p'=i(t)p$. The local-lifting hypothesis gives an fppf covering $\{V_a\to U\}$ and $p_a\in P(V_a)$. Thus the fibre has a simply transitive action wherever it has sections; no surjectivity on $C$-points has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 03P8, theorem-picard-group, expanded by coordinate descent; groupoids.tex, lemma-characterize-trivial-pseudo-torsors and definition-principal-homogeneous-space

proof.text: On $V_{ab}=V_a\times_UV_b$, write $p_b=i(g_{ab})p_a$ for the unique $g_{ab}\in T(V_{ab})$. The group law gives $g_{ac}=g_{bc}g_{ab}$ on triple overlaps. Each coordinate $g_{ab,h}$ is a unit of $\Gamma(V_{ab},\mathcal O)$, for $1\leq h\leq r$. The fppf covering is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. For each $h$, multiplication by $g_{ab,h}$ specifies descent data on the modules $\mathcal O_{V_a}$: equivalently, their local frames are to satisfy $e_{b,h}=g_{ab,h}e_{a,h}$. The displayed cocycle is exactly the descent condition. Part 3 of [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] therefore gives an invertible $\mathcal O_U$-module $L_h$ and compatible frames $e_{a,h}$ of its pullbacks. This is coordinatewise effective descent, not an invocation of a torus-torsor classification theorem.

source.place: Tag 03P8, theorem-picard-group, expanded by coordinate descent; groupoids.tex, lemma-characterize-trivial-pseudo-torsors and definition-principal-homogeneous-space

proof.text: Every $L_h$ is trivial on $U$. Indeed, by the definition of an invertible module it is trivial on an open neighbourhood $W$ of the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $C$. Choose a basic open $D(f)$ with $\mathfrak m\in D(f)\subseteq W$. Then $f\notin\mathfrak m$, hence $f$ is a unit: a nonunit generates a proper ideal contained in a maximal ideal, which must be $\mathfrak m$. Thus $D(f)=U$ and $W=U$. Choose a global frame $v_h$ of $L_h$. On $V_a$ write $v_h=u_{a,h}e_{a,h}$ with $u_{a,h}\in\Gamma(V_a,\mathcal O)^{\times}$. On overlaps the frame relation gives $u_{a,h}=g_{ab,h}u_{b,h}$. Let $u_a=(u_{a,h})_h\in T(V_a)$.

source.place: Tag 03P8, theorem-picard-group, expanded by coordinate descent; groupoids.tex, lemma-characterize-trivial-pseudo-torsors and definition-principal-homogeneous-space

proof.text: Put $z_a=i(u_a)p_a\in E(V_a)$. On $V_{ab}$ one has $z_b=i(u_b)i(g_{ab})p_a=i(u_a)p_a=z_a$, since $u_a=g_{ab}u_b$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to the fpqc cover from step 2 and the compatible morphisms $z_a:V_a\to E$ to obtain $z:U\to E$. Uniqueness in that same descent statement, applied to the targets $U$ and $J$, shows that $z$ is over $U$ and $qz=j$, since both equalities hold on the cover. Thus $z\in E(C)$ lifts $j$. For $r=0$ the tuple of modules and units is empty, $T$ is the trivial group, and the same calculation says that the original local lifts agree and descend. Fields are nonzero local rings, so the stated field case follows.

tool_uses.why: Use part 3 to descend the rank-one coordinate modules for an fpqc covering of Spec C. This is a generic descent tool; the unit supplies no such module-descent statement, and the field-base torus-frame lemma does not cover arbitrary local rings.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q101-1fa33812d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the base copy, all 7 cited statements and the Stacks sources at the cited places. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from the base, which was unsplit with no proof. There are no new nodes. Step 1: the fibre P=E×_{J,j}U is a T-pseudo-torsor with fppf-local sections, by the kernel identification and the lifting hypothesis. Step 2: g_ac=g_bc g_ab is checked. Coordinatewise unit cocycles become effective descent data by lem-pc-fpqc-descent part 3 (Stacks 023T, descent.tex l.1584), applied to the cover, which is fpqc by 022C (topologies.tex l.3044). Step 3: on Spec of a local ring an invertible module is trivial by the D(f) argument; the orientation u_a=g_ab u_b is checked. Step 4: z_a=i(u_a)p_a are compatible. lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent glues them to z, and its uniqueness for targets U and J gives that z is a U-point with qz=j. I checked r=0, fields, and nonreduced and non-noetherian C. Route: the only off-unit citation that is not a Mathlib leaf is lem-pc-fpqc-descent, a generic black-box descent tool. It is declared in tool_uses and I accept it. Batch-5 flag on lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc: it is a Mathlib leaf saying fppf coverings are fpqc (Stacks 022C, unit sk-i-curve-zero, no proof_deps). This is general topology, not given by either assumption and not part of the proof of the trace formula or of Poincaré duality, so I accept it. No duplicates: lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-frame-geometry needs a field base, and thm-sc-hilbert-90 and lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor cover only the Zariski and étale sites. No SGA is used. No fixes.
